title: F-35B Lightning II (short take-off / vertical landing)

sources.title: Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II (Wikipedia), cockpit and variants
What is good and bad about the F-35 cockpit (Hush-Kit, pilot interview)
JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: The F-35B is the version that can take off from short decks and land straight down, like the Harrier: a lift fan behind the cockpit and a swivelling engine nozzle push it up. Its cockpit is that of the F-35A plus the STOVL mode, in which the flight computer turns the stick and throttle into hover commands; there is no separate nozzle lever and no gun built in. This guide follows the F-35A guide.

panels.name: Side-stick
panels.text: A side-stick on the right console instead of a centre stick, with the trigger and the weapon release button.
panels.context: Its HOTAS switch layout is not public; only the stick, trigger and release are listed.

controls.name: Side-stick
controls.text: The stick on the right console. In normal flight it rolls and pitches the aircraft. In the STOVL mode (short take-off and vertical landing) the flight computer turns its movements into commands for the flight path and speed, and for banking or sliding sideways in the hover.
controls.context: Thanks to this 'unified' control the F-35B needs no nozzle lever like the Harrier; the computer works the lift fan and the swivelling nozzle.

controls.name: Trigger
controls.text: The trigger at the front of the side-stick. Pulling it fires the gun pod under the fuselage; the F-35B has no gun built in.
controls.context: It only fires when the weapons are armed with the master arm switch; the HUD or sight shows where the shots will go.

panels.name: Throttle
panels.text: The single throttle on the left console.
panels.context: Its switches are not public; only the thrust function is listed.

controls.name: Throttle (active inceptor)
controls.text: The lever that sets the engine power, like a car's gas pedal, in normal flight. In the STOVL mode the flight computer turns it into a vertical speed command: forward climbs, back sinks.
controls.context: The pilot does not manage the lift fan and nozzle himself; the computer does it from the throttle and stick commands.
